newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus to bid for China 100-plane order.
newsitem.headline: Airbus to bid for China 100-plane order.

text.p: European aircraft consortium Airbus Industrie has put in a bid for China's requirement for 100 narrow-body passenger aircraft, estimated to be worth around $5 billion, an industry source said on Tuesday.
Airbus "have put in a bid", said the source, adding that it does not expect the whole order, which may be split with U.S. rivals, Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.

China has a number of major regional companies clamouring for new aircraft, to keep up with traffic growth. But purchases are centralised and there appear to be negotiations "between the centre and the periphery", the source said.
Any decision to buy Airbus planes is not expected before an official visit to China by French President Jacques Chirac in May, when an announcement would have a highly symbolic gesture.

But U.S. Vice President Al Gore is also due to visit China in late March, for which high-powered diplomatic efforts have been made to prepare multi-billion dollar contracts. Undersecretary of commerce Stuart Eizenstat and Secretary of State Madeleine Albright have been enlisted in the campaign.
Boeing has held the lion's share of the Chinese market historically in the past 25-plus years, with one out of every 10 planes made being sold to Chinese airlines in the last three years.
Boeing forecasts China and Hong Kong will need 1,900 passenger aircraft in the next 20 years, worth $124 billion.
But Airbus believes it has a strong claim in the Chinese market, with a backlog of deliveries of 38 Airbus planes.

It secured a commercial and political coup last April during an official visit to France by Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng, when the Chinese authorities ordered 30 Airbus planes and signed a deal to work on a new 100-seater jet with a European group.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
